Get started with cd2030.core

Source: vignettes/cd2030.core.Rmd
cd2030.core.Rmd

cd2030.core is the Countdown to 2030 analysis of routine health facility data. This guide loads a dataset, looks at its quality, computes coverage and saves the work, in about twenty lines of R. Each step has its own guide with the detail:

Step Guide
What a dataset file must contain vignette("preparing-data")
Reporting rates, outliers, missing values, consistency vignette("data-quality")
Adjustment, denominators, coverage, reports vignette("coverage")
The Shiny apps built on this package vignette("building-an-app")

Install

The package is published on r-universe, not CRAN. datasuite.ui, which it needs, is in the same repository.

install.packages(
  "cd2030.core",
  repos = c("https://damurka.r-universe.dev", "https://alkemalab.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)

Add dependencies = TRUE for the optional features: PDF and PowerPoint export, and the Bayesian coverage model.

Load a dataset

A dataset is the Countdown Excel workbook, a Stata .dta master file, or an .rds saved by this package. The package comes with an example workbook for Kenya.

library(cd2030.core)

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
cache <- load_cache_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths, ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah

Loading reads the sheets, cleans the column names, merges them into one table with a row per district and month, and works out which indicator group the file holds ("rmncah" or "vaccine"). It also names the columns that are empty.

cache is a CacheConnection: the data together with every choice made about it (years removed, adjustment factors, denominators, surveys). The data itself is a tibble of class cd_data.

data <- cache$countdown_data
data

For the country it found, the package fills in the reference data it holds: UN population estimates, WUENIC immunization estimates and the household surveys.

cache$country
#> [1] "Kenya"
cache$survey_years
#> [1] 2014 2022

If you only want the data, load_data(path) returns the cd_data tibble without the CacheConnection.

Look at the quality of the data

The quality functions take the data and return a table. Most take an administrative level: "national", "adminlevel_1" (region) or "district".

calculate_average_reporting_rate(data)
#> # Table 1a: Annual average reporting rates for all indicators, by year
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>    year anc_rr idelv_rr vacc_rr opd_rr mean_rr
#>   <int>  <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1  2019     94       94      94     95      94
#> 2  2020     96       96      95     96      96
#> 3  2021     96       96      96     96      96
#> 4  2022     97       97      97     96      97
#> 5  2023     97       97      98     97      97

Most results have a plot() method.

plot(calculate_district_reporting_rate(data, threshold = 90))

calculate_overall_score() puts the checks in one table: completeness, extreme outliers, consistency between related indicators, and a score for each year.

calculate_overall_score(data, threshold = 90)[, c("no", "Data Quality Metrics", "2022", "2023")]
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>    no    `Data Quality Metrics`                                       `2022` `2023`
#>    <chr> <chr>                                                         <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 1a    % of expected monthly facility reports (national)             96.4   96.9 
#>  2 1b    % of districts with completeness of facility reporting >= 90  93     96   
#>  3 1c    % of districts with no missing values for the 4 forms         84.0   84.7 
#>  4 2a    % of monthly values that are not extreme outliers (national)  98.8   96.1 
#>  5 2b    % of districts with no extreme outliers in the year           91.7   87.2 
#>  6 3a    Ratio anc1/penta1                                              1.07   1.06
#>  7 3b    Ratio penta1/penta3                                            1.04   1.04
#>  8 3c    % district with anc1/penta1 in expected ranged                87.2   85.1 
#>  9 3d    % district with penta1/penta3 in expected ranged              87.2   93.6 
#> 10 4     Annual data quality score                                     91.2   91.4

Adjust the data and compute coverage

Coverage is computed from adjusted data: counts scaled up for incomplete reporting, with extreme outliers and missing values replaced. The CacheConnection does this with the settings it holds and keeps the result.

cache$set_k_factors(c(anc = 0.25, idelv = 0.25, vacc = 0.25, opd = 0.25, ipd = 0.25))
cache$adjust_data()

Coverage also needs a few national rates. Those the country’s latest survey has are already filled in; this survey has no stillbirth rate, so it is given here.

cache$set_national_estimates(list(sbr = 0.02))

coverage <- cache$get_filtered_coverage("penta3", "national")
coverage
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   estimates        `2014` `2019` `2020` `2021` `2022` `2023`
#>   <chr>             <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 DHIS2 estimate     NA     92.2   93.2   92.1   93.8   93.7
#> 2 Survey estimates   89.9   NA     NA     NA     89.2   NA  
#> 3 95% CI LL          88.5   NA     NA     NA     87.8   NA  
#> 4 95% CI UL          91.1   NA     NA     NA     90.4   NA  
#> 5 WUENIC estimates   NA     91     89     91     90     93

The table sets the facility-data estimate beside the survey and WUENIC estimates, and so does its chart.

plot(coverage)

Save the work

Give the dataset a path and it saves itself there, now and after each later change. load_cache_data() opens the file again with every choice as it was.

saved <- file.path(tempdir(), "kenya.rds")
cache$set_cache_path(saved)
#> ℹ Successfully saved to "/tmp/RtmpXh91H8/kenya.rds".

reopened <- load_cache_data(saved)
reopened$k_factors
#>   anc idelv  vacc   opd   ipd 
#>  0.25  0.25  0.25  0.25  0.25

Where to go next

  • vignette("preparing-data") describes the workbook and how to check your own file.
  • vignette("data-quality") and vignette("coverage") follow the analysis step by step.
  • The reference lists every function by analysis step. ?CacheConnection lists everything the dataset object holds and computes.
  • The same analysis is available without writing R in the Countdown apps (cd2030.rmncah, cd2030.vaxx), which run inside DataSuite. vignette("building-an-app") describes how they are built.
